buckets.title: Chemical Bonding and Hybridisation
buckets.badge_reason: The central difficulty is coordinating spatial 3D stereochemical representation with steric domain definitions and orbital conservation.

capabilities.action: Inventory central-atom steric electron domains by grouping multiple bonds into single domains and including only central lone pairs
capabilities.success_criterion: Count bonded atoms and central lone pairs accurately without counting terminal lone pairs or inflating double/triple bonds

capabilities.action: Map steric electron domain counts to introductory hybrid-orbital sets (sp, sp2, sp3) and classify coaxial vs lateral orbital overlaps
capabilities.success_criterion: Apply orbital conservation (n atomic orbitals mix to yield n hybrid orbitals) and distinguish cylindrical sigma symmetry from nodal pi symmetry

capabilities.action: Translate flat Lewis connectivity sketches into 3D wedge-dash stereochemical representations and evaluate qualitative models
capabilities.success_criterion: Accurately depict 3D tetrahedral bond angles (109.5° / 107°) with wedge-dash notation and evaluate VSEPR predictive scope vs orbital overlap boundaries

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Separate a bonded-atom direction from the number of shared pairs.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: The sigma component and pi component of a multiple bond connect the same atom pair.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Circle the distinct neighbours of carbon, then keep an independent bond-component inventory.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: HCHO carbon has three bonded-atom directions. C=O contributes one local domain, although its double bond contains one sigma and one pi component. Pi density is not confined to the internuclear axis.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: a triple bond to N in HCN still supplies one C-to-N direction; carbon also has the H direction.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: At carbon in HCN, count bonded-atom directions and C-N shared pairs separately. Repeat the two counts for HCHO.
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: HCN: two carbon directions, three C-N pairs. HCHO: three directions, two C-O pairs. Repeated multiplicity-as-direction counting suggests the misconception.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Explain why replacing a double bond with a triple bond to the same neighbour need not add a direction.

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: The counting centre is nitrogen, not every atom in NF3.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: Local domains consist of bonds and lone pairs at the selected atom.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Circle nitrogen before counting; keep terminal-fluorine pairs in a separate inventory.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: NF3 has three nitrogen-to-fluorine directions and one nitrogen lone pair: four N-centred domains. Terminal F lone pairs do not add N-centred domains.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: substituting H for F leaves the local three-bond-plus-lone-pair N inventory unchanged in the introductory model.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Count N-centred domains in NH3 and NF3. Then state where the F lone pairs are located.
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: Both N centres have four domains; F pairs are located at F. Repeated inclusion of terminal pairs identifies locality confusion.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Count domains at oxygen in H2O while excluding electrons assigned to H.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: Terminal-atom lone pairs add domains at the central atom.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q8

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Critique the counting operation, rather than merely giving a corrected label.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: Bond multiplicity and neighbour directions are different ledgers.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Show the faulty ledger beside a neighbour-only ledger; complete the corrected count yourself.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Counting both C=O lines as separate domains confuses bond components with one bonded-atom direction. HCHO carbon has three domains.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: HCN carbon has two neighbour directions even though C-N is triple.

microtopics.title: Steric electron-domain counting and multiple bonds
microtopics.badge_reason: Multiple bonds and terminal lone pairs frequently trigger incorrect steric number counts.
entry_assumptions: Recognises single and multiple bonds in simple Lewis structures.
microtopics.inferential_jump: HCHO carbon has three bonded-atom directions. C=O contributes one local domain, although its double bond contains one sigma and one pi component. Pi density is not confined to the internuclear axis.

teaching_path.action: Make separate neighbour and shared-pair inventories for HCHO.
teaching_path.why_valid: Two H atoms and one O are attached to C; a C=O double bond contains two shared pairs.
inputs: The Lewis structure H2C=O has a double bond from carbon to oxygen and one single bond from carbon to each hydrogen. Explain why the C=O double bond counts as one electron domain around carbon.
teaching_path.output: Three neighbours; two pairs in C=O.

teaching_path.action: Count C-to-O as one local VSEPR domain.
teaching_path.why_valid: A multiple bond connects one pair of nuclei and supplies one bonded-neighbour direction in local domain counting. Sigma and pi density have different spatial symmetry.
inputs: Three neighbours; two pairs in C=O.
teaching_path.output: One C=O domain; this does not place pi density on the internuclear axis.

teaching_path.action: Add the two C-H directions.
teaching_path.why_valid: Each of the two distinct C-H connections adds one domain and C has no lone pair.
inputs: One C=O domain; this does not place pi density on the internuclear axis.
teaching_path.output: 1+1+1 = three C-centred domains.

teaching_path.action: Recount carbon directions in HCN.
teaching_path.why_valid: H-C and C-N connect carbon to two neighbours although C-N has three shared pairs.
inputs: 1+1+1 = three C-centred domains.
teaching_path.output: Two domains in HCN; shared-pair count and neighbour count are different.

teaching_path.action: Choose nitrogen as the counting centre.
teaching_path.why_valid: The requested domains are centred on N, not on the entire NF3 molecule.
inputs: A nitrogen atom in NF3 has three N–F single bonds and one lone pair. Each fluorine also has lone pairs. Count the electron domains around nitrogen and state which lone pairs belong in that central-atom count.
teaching_path.output: Three N-F bonding directions are included.

teaching_path.action: Assign each lone pair to its own atom.
teaching_path.why_valid: N has one lone pair; terminal F lone pairs belong to F-centred inventories.
inputs: Three N-F bonding directions are included.
teaching_path.output: One N lone pair included; terminal F lone pairs excluded from the N count.

teaching_path.action: Add the local entries.
teaching_path.why_valid: The N inventory has three bonded directions plus one central lone pair.
inputs: One N lone pair included; terminal F lone pairs excluded from the N count.
teaching_path.output: 3+1 = four nitrogen-centred domains.

teaching_path.action: Substitute H for F in the local comparison.
teaching_path.why_valid: NH3 has the same three-bond/one-central-pair N inventory even though terminal atoms differ.
inputs: 3+1 = four nitrogen-centred domains.
teaching_path.output: NH3 also has four N domains; terminal pairs were not required for that total.

teaching_path.action: Identify the faulty C=O line-counting entry.
teaching_path.why_valid: Two drawn bond lines denote two bond components to one O neighbour.
inputs: A student counts the double bond in H2C=O as two separate directions and predicts four domains around carbon. Locate the counting error and give the corrected domain count.
teaching_path.output: The student counted one neighbour twice.

teaching_path.action: Replace bond-line counting with local neighbour counting.
teaching_path.why_valid: In VSEPR a multiple bond supplies one bonded-neighbour domain; pi density is lateral rather than an extra atom direction.
inputs: The student counted one neighbour twice.
teaching_path.output: C=O contributes one domain, not two.

teaching_path.action: Compute the corrected HCHO total.
teaching_path.why_valid: There are two distinct H neighbours, one O neighbour and no C lone pair.
inputs: C=O contributes one domain, not two.
teaching_path.output: 2+1+0 = three C-centred domains.

teaching_path.action: Apply the operation to CO2.
teaching_path.why_valid: Two C=O bonds connect C to two O neighbours; four drawn bond lines do not imply four local domains.
inputs: 2+1+0 = three C-centred domains.
teaching_path.output: CO2 carbon has two domains in the introductory model.

exit_task.prompt: At carbon in CO2, count local domains and then separately count the shared pairs in both C=O bonds. Explain why the totals differ.

answer.summary: Two carbon-neighbour domains; four shared pairs. Each double bond connects one O neighbour.
reasoning: Two carbon-neighbour domains; four shared pairs. Each double bond connects one O neighbour.

predict.prompt: Does a C=O double bond count as two separate directions around carbon?
predict.defensible_answer: No; both pairs share the same internuclear coordinate line and act as one domain.

attempt.produces: A domain inventory distinguishing bonded atoms from individual electron pairs.

rubric.criterion: Treats double bond as 1 domain and excludes terminal lone pairs.
rubric.evidence_of: Understands spatial definition of electron domains.

accepted: Double bond = 1 domain; only central lone pairs count.
rejected: Include terminal fluorine lone pairs in central count.

task.prompt: List the bonding domains and central lone pairs for H2C=O.

route.ask: How many distinct atoms are attached to the central carbon?
route.why_this_ask: Each attached atom defines one bonding domain.

boundary_test.prompt: If a triple bond is present instead of a double bond, how many domains does it count as?
boundary_test.answer: Exactly one domain; all shared pairs occupy the same internuclear space.
boundary_test.confirms: Domain count depends on bonded atom direction, not bond multiplicity.

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Distinguish the hybrid-set name from the number of orbitals in that set.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: A change of orbital basis preserves the number of independent orbitals.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Write one valence s plus n valence p orbitals; determine n and the resulting set size yourself.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: For second-period atoms, one 2s plus three 2p orbitals gives four sp3 hybrids. The superscript counts p inputs, not total outputs.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: an sp set has two hybrids because one s plus one p supplies two basis functions; use this conservation rule on the requested set.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: An sp2 set is proposed to contain two hybrids. How many input and output orbitals should it have? Then apply your method to an sp set.
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: Three for sp2, two for sp. Repeating the superscript-as-total rule in both cases suggests a held counting rule; correct changed cases after an isolated slip suggest an execution error.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Give the input/output inventory for sp without copying the original set.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: The superscript is the total number of hybrid orbitals.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q1

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: The task asks for a local count before the introductory geometry label.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: Four bonding directions and no central lone pair use the demonstrated four-domain rule.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Inventory only carbon-centred domains; attach the known rule without reading shape from page angles.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: CH4 has four bonding domains, no carbon lone pair, and a tetrahedral introductory sp3 description. A Lewis layout encodes connectivity.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: CH3Cl still has four bonded neighbours around carbon even if the bonds have different properties.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Count domains at C in CH3Cl and C in CH4. Does redrawing either as a cross change its count?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: Both have four; changing drawing placement changes neither connectivity nor domain count. Repeated drawing-angle dependence suggests a spatial-model error.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Classify carbon in CH2Cl2 by domain inventory, not bond identity.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: The page layout is the molecular geometry.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q3

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Use the stated internuclear axis to classify the overlap.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: End-on and side-on are orientation/symmetry descriptions, not molecule-name clues.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Locate the axis and the density above/below it; name the two classes yourself.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Sigma overlap is end-on/axial in the supplied sketch; pi overlap is lateral with a nodal plane containing the axis.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: rotating the entire sketch on the page leaves its classification unchanged relative to the rotated axis.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Rotate the whole end-on sketch by 90 degrees on paper. Does it become pi? Compare that with rotating one p orbital relative to its neighbour.
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: Whole-picture rotation does not change sigma/pi classification; relative orbital rotation can change overlap. Conflating page orientation with relative geometry suggests the misconception.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Label a sigma component within a triple bond using its geometry.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: Turning a drawing on the page changes sigma into pi.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q6

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Map each set name to an orbital inventory, not its superscript alone.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: One s plus n p inputs gives n+1 hybrid outputs.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Write separate input/output ledgers for BF3 and CH4 before matching labels.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: BF3: three domains and three sp2 hybrids. CH4: four domains and four sp3 hybrids. For these centres use valence 2s/2p language rather than ambiguous 1s + 2p shorthand.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: sp uses two inputs and two hybrid outputs, providing a third case for the conservation rule.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Compare proposed totals sp=1, sp2=2, sp3=3 against basis-function conservation. Give the corrected sequence.
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: The corrected sequence is 2,3,4. Repeating the shifted sequence suggests the superscript-as-total rule.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Reconstruct all three set sizes without memorising the sequence.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: sp2 has two hybrids and sp3 has three.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q10

microtopics.title: Hybridisation, orbital conservation, and overlap symmetry
microtopics.badge_reason: Learners must correlate domain counts with conserved hybrid sets and classify overlap symmetry.
entry_assumptions: Understands basic s and p atomic orbital shapes.
microtopics.inferential_jump: BF3: three domains and three sp2 hybrids. CH4: four domains and four sp3 hybrids. For these centres use valence 2s/2p language rather than ambiguous 1s + 2p shorthand.

teaching_path.action: Read the requested four equivalent domain directions.
teaching_path.why_valid: The question supplies a tetrahedral four-direction introductory model.
inputs: In the introductory valence-bond model, name the hybrid-orbital set used for four equivalent electron-domain directions around a central atom, and state how many hybrid orbitals it contains.
teaching_path.output: Four model directions must be represented.

teaching_path.action: Select one valence s and three valence p inputs.
teaching_path.why_valid: For a second-period centre, these four independent basis functions can be recombined without changing the basis dimension.
inputs: Four model directions must be represented.
teaching_path.output: 2s + 2px + 2py + 2pz: four inputs.

teaching_path.action: Name the recombined set and count its members.
teaching_path.why_valid: The name sp3 records one s and three p inputs; the total number is 1+3.
inputs: 2s + 2px + 2py + 2pz: four inputs.
teaching_path.output: sp3; four hybrid orbitals.

teaching_path.action: Compare the count with an sp allocation.
teaching_path.why_valid: One s plus one p has two outputs, so the superscript alone cannot be the set size.
inputs: sp3; four hybrid orbitals.
teaching_path.output: sp has two outputs; the four-member sp3 inventory is consistent.

teaching_path.action: Inventory CH4 at carbon.
teaching_path.why_valid: The supplied Lewis connectivity has four C-H bonds and no C lone pair.
inputs: For CH4, use the known rule for four bonding domains and no central lone pair to assign the carbon hybridisation and electron-domain geometry. Show the domain count.
teaching_path.output: Four bonding domains; zero central lone pairs.

teaching_path.action: Apply the explicitly supplied four-domain rule.
teaching_path.why_valid: The task asks for the known introductory correspondence, rather than an experimental determination of orbital coefficients.
inputs: Four bonding domains; zero central lone pairs.
teaching_path.output: Tetrahedral domain geometry; introductory sp3 description.

teaching_path.action: Check the orbital basis ledger.
teaching_path.why_valid: One 2s plus three 2p inputs gives four hybrids, matching four model sigma directions.
inputs: Tetrahedral domain geometry; introductory sp3 description.
teaching_path.output: Four inputs and four outputs; no residual p in this allocation.

teaching_path.action: Change one substituent without adding a neighbour.
teaching_path.why_valid: CH3Cl still has four carbon-neighbour connections; different bond properties do not constitute extra domains.
inputs: Four inputs and four outputs; no residual p in this allocation.
teaching_path.output: CH3Cl also has four C-centred domains; no exact bond-property claim follows.

teaching_path.action: Mark the line joining the nuclei in each sketch.
teaching_path.why_valid: Sigma/pi labels refer to overlap relative to this internuclear axis, not to page orientation.
inputs: For a qualitative orbital sketch, overlap A is end-on along the internuclear axis and overlap B is side-on on opposite sides of that axis. Classify each as sigma or pi overlap and identify the defining feature you used.
teaching_path.output: A common geometric reference is declared.

teaching_path.action: Classify A from its stated end-on overlap.
teaching_path.why_valid: The supplied overlap is axial; in the introductory sketch the sigma component is symmetric about the bond axis.
inputs: A common geometric reference is declared.
teaching_path.output: A is sigma overlap.

teaching_path.action: Classify B from side-on p overlap.
teaching_path.why_valid: The supplied parallel lateral lobes have a nodal plane containing the axis.
inputs: A is sigma overlap.
teaching_path.output: B is pi overlap.

teaching_path.action: Rotate the whole picture, including its axis.
teaching_path.why_valid: A rigid rotation preserves all relative orientation and symmetry relations.
inputs: B is pi overlap.
teaching_path.output: Neither classification changes under whole-picture rotation.

teaching_path.action: Read the two supplied domain inventories.
teaching_path.why_valid: The task supplies three B bonding domains and four C bonding domains, with no central lone pairs.
inputs: The benchmark supplies this table: BF3 has three bonding domains and no central lone pair; CH4 has four bonding domains and no central lone pair. Match each central atom to the introductory sp2 or sp3 model, and check that the number of hybrid-orbital directions agrees with the domain count.
teaching_path.output: BF3: three; CH4: four.

teaching_path.action: Match each inventory to a conserved valence-basis allocation.
teaching_path.why_valid: One s plus two p yields three hybrids; one s plus three p yields four.
inputs: BF3: three; CH4: four.
teaching_path.output: BF3: sp2, three hybrids; CH4: sp3, four hybrids.

teaching_path.action: Match the ideal domain arrangement within this introductory model.
teaching_path.why_valid: Three equivalent model directions are planar; four are tetrahedral. These labels are model descriptions.
inputs: BF3: sp2, three hybrids; CH4: sp3, four hybrids.
teaching_path.output: BF3: trigonal planar; CH4: tetrahedral.

teaching_path.action: Reconstruct an sp inventory as a third case.
teaching_path.why_valid: One s plus one p provides two inputs and therefore two hybrid outputs.
inputs: BF3: trigonal planar; CH4: tetrahedral.
teaching_path.output: The set-size sequence is sp=2, sp2=3, sp3=4, rather than the superscripts 1,2,3.

question_families.title: Steric electron-domain counting and multiple-bond constraints
solution_structure: Locate the central atom and identify all attached bonded atoms.
Treat single, double, or triple bonds to an attached atom as exactly one bonding domain.
Count unshared lone pairs residing directly on the central atom; exclude terminal lone pairs.
Sum bonding domains and central lone pairs to obtain total steric number.

demand_dimensions.model_choice: Distinguish electron pair count from steric spatial domain count.
demand_dimensions.representation_translation: Translate Lewis structural formulas into steric domain groupings.
demand_dimensions.reasoning_steps: Inventory bonded atoms, add central lone pairs, verify exclusion of terminal lone pairs.
demand_dimensions.novelty: Multiple bonds (double/triple) and peripheral lone pairs as intentional distractors.

safe_variations: Change central atom or ligand atoms while preserving steric number rules.
transfer_boundaries: Odd-electron free radicals or hypervalent expanded octets require advanced extensions.
common_wrong_routes: Count double bonds as two domains or add terminal halogen lone pairs to the central atom count.

question_families.title: Hybrid-orbital mapping, orbital symmetry, and 3D stereochemical representation
solution_structure: Determine total electron domains from steric inventory.
Map domain count to hybrid set (2->sp, 3->sp2, 4->sp3) using orbital conservation.
Represent non-coplanar 3D geometry using wedge-dash notation (two in-plane, one wedge, one dash).
Classify orbital overlaps (sigma vs pi) and evaluate predictive boundaries of VSEPR vs orbital models.

demand_dimensions.model_choice: Select between VSEPR geometric repulsion and Valence Bond orbital overlap.
demand_dimensions.representation_translation: Translate flat 2D Lewis sketches into 3D wedge-dash stereochemical structures.
demand_dimensions.reasoning_steps: Determine steric domains, select hybrid set, construct 3D representation, check symmetry/angles.
demand_dimensions.novelty: Distinguishing what VSEPR predicts (geometry) from what it leaves unresolved (wave mechanics).

safe_variations: Vary steric numbers 2, 3, and 4 and compare coaxial vs lateral overlap scenarios.
transfer_boundaries: d-orbital participation in hypervalent molecules is omitted in introductory models.
common_wrong_routes: Assume 4 domains produce 90-degree square planar geometry on flat paper.

items.title: Orbital overlap planes in allene (H2C=C=CH2)
items.prompt: In propadiene (allene, H2C=C=CH2), the central carbon atom forms two double bonds. Identify the hybridisation of the central carbon and deduce whether the two terminal CH2 groups lie in the same plane or in mutually perpendicular planes. Support your conclusion using orbital overlap symmetry.
items.source_label: Original competition-style transfer; not claimed as an official past-paper item.

answer.summary: The central carbon is sp hybridized, and the two terminal CH2 groups lie in mutually perpendicular planes.
reasoning: The central carbon has 2 bonding domains and 0 lone pairs, giving sp hybridisation with a linear 180° C-C-C backbone.
The central carbon has two unhybridized 2p orbitals (say, 2py and 2pz) that are mutually orthogonal (at 90° to each other).
One double bond is formed by lateral overlap with a 2py orbital of the left carbon, while the other double bond is formed by lateral overlap with a 2pz orbital of the right carbon.
Because the two pi bonds are oriented in perpendicular planes, the sigma frameworks and terminal CH2 groups must also be oriented in mutually perpendicular planes.

items.title: Nitrogen hybridisation in formamide and lone pair delocalisation
items.prompt: In an isolated amine (such as NH3), nitrogen is sp3 hybridized with a pyramidal geometry. In formamide (HCONH2), however, the nitrogen atom is experimentally observed to be nearly planar. Using electron domain and resonance arguments, explain why nitrogen's lone pair changes its effective steric behavior and hybridisation.
items.source_label: Original competition-style transfer; not claimed as an official past-paper item.

answer.summary: The nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the adjacent C=O carbonyl pi system via resonance, requiring nitrogen to adopt sp2 hybridisation and planar geometry.
reasoning: The nitrogen lone pair participates in resonance: H2N-CH=O <-> H2N+=CH-O-.
For resonance overlap to occur, nitrogen's non-bonding pair must occupy an unhybridized 2p orbital parallel to the carbonyl pi bond.
This re-hybridizes nitrogen from sp3 to sp2, leaving three in-plane sigma bonding directions (trigonal planar, ~120°) and one perpendicular p orbital containing the delocalised pair.
